sql:
SELECT cls,
       COUNT(*) AS n_trips,
       SUM(anglers) AS anglers,
       SUM(yt) AS yt,
       SUM(yt)/NULLIF(SUM(anglers),0) AS rate,
       AVG(CASE WHEN yt>0 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS pct_nonzero_trips
FROM trips
WHERE cls IN ('hd_am','hd_pm','hd_unspecified','hd_twilight','three_quarter','full_day','overnight','day_1_5')
GROUP BY cls
ORDER BY rate DESC

SELECT cls, COUNT(*) n, SUM(anglers) anglers, SUM(yt) yt, SUM(yt)/NULLIF(SUM(anglers),0) rate
FROM trips WHERE cls IN ('hd_night','multi_day') GROUP BY cls

summary: Added a class-viability filter (all-time pooled yt/angler must clear 0.05 with >=200 sampled anglers) before a class can be booked at all, and fixed twilight bookings to use twilight's own trailing rate instead of the pooled cheap-class rate. Data showed hd_am/hd_pm ~0.005 and hd_twilight exactly 0.0 all season (vs three_quarter 0.166, overnight 0.35, day_1_5 0.83) - the old logic was chasing noise on dead classes (e.g. booking twilight off a three_quarter hot streak, guaranteed skunk) and burning budget on near-zero-EV half-day bets, which is likely why budget ran out by day 214 before any late-season window could be played.
